liquidity_funding.text: Cash and cash-like investments were stable at {{cash_like@FY2025}}, a change of {{cash_like.change@FY2025}}, and cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, below the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2025}}.

Debt due within one year rose by {{debt_due_1y.change@FY2025}} to {{debt_due_1y@FY2025}}, so cash liquidity covers the near-term maturities only thinly, and in FY2024 borrowings due within two years were {{borrowings_due_2y@FY2024}}.

Free cash flow after lease payments was {{fcf_after_leases@FY2024}} in FY2024, or {{fcf_after_leases_to_debt@FY2024}} of debt, showing that lease payments absorbed the cash that free cash flow leaves out.

Customer prepayments rose, with contract liabilities up {{contract_liabilities.change@FY2025}} to {{contract_liabilities@FY2025}} and advance ticket cover up by {{advance_ticket_cover.change@FY2025}} to {{advance_ticket_cover@FY2025}}, the lowest of the peer group.

watch_items.text: Liquidity: cash liquidity to revenue fell by {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.change@FY2025}} to {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue@FY2025}}, below the peer median of {{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_median@FY2025}}, the weakest of the group ({{cash_liquidity_to_revenue.peer_rank@FY2025}}).

Maturities: debt due within one year rose by {{debt_due_1y.change@FY2025}} to {{debt_due_1y@FY2025}}, against cash and cash-like investments of {{cash_like@FY2025}}, so refinancing needs are met from a thinner cash buffer.

Cash generation: FCF to debt of {{fcf_to_debt@FY2025}} is below the peer median of {{fcf_to_debt.peer_median@FY2025}} and the weakest of the group ({{fcf_to_debt.peer_rank@FY2025}}), with capex intensity at {{capex_intensity@FY2025}} above the peer median of {{capex_intensity.peer_median@FY2025}}.
Funding: the group placed senior unsecured bonds under its EMTN programme and redeemed its hybrid bonds, while extending the maturity of its revolving credit facility to 2029.
